title: feat(route): name why a guard lane is held, and await a round, in the route stdouts
description:
## .what

two gaps in the guard round stdout, each paved locally in uladkasach/dev-env-setup (PR #167) as a repo skill. build both into the extant route stdouts, then the local skills retire.

### 1. a held lane names no reason — local skill `route.guard.lanes.get`

a guard round that pours no lane prints only the held verdicts. it never says WHY each lane was held. the local skill replays the guard inputs, read-only, per peer lane:

- the artifact hash, and the givens at that hash (`iN:exitClass` per lane)
- the latest given at the hash vs the cached given the guard reads (`getAllCachedPassedReviews` → `getOneCacheSafePeerReviewArtifact`)
- the meter (rounds/budget) and the level latch (`getStoneGuardLevelsPoured`)
- the pre-gate verdict (`computeReviewPeerVerdict`)

it is how #711 was found: a lane whose latest given refused was served an older passed verdict, so the judge held it on a residual no stance could clear.

fix shape: `route.stone.set --as arrived` and `route.drive` print, per held lane, `cached iN vs latest iM` and the verdict cause — or add `route.guard.lanes.get` to the driver role.

### 2. no bounded wait for a round — local skill `route.guard.round.await`

a round with expensive lanes (an l3 `rhx enroll`) runs many minutes, and givens land only as each lane ends. a driver polls by hand and spends turns. the local skill waits once, bounded (default 1200s), for N givens at iteration I, and names which slugs landed; exit 2 names the ones that landed if the bound passes first.

fix shape: an `--await` on `route.stone.set --as arrived`, or a driver skill `route.guard.round.await`.

## .source

- https://github.com/uladkasach/dev-env-setup/pull/167 (review comment on `route.guard.lanes.get.sh`)
- `.agent/repo=.this/role=any/skills/route.guard.lanes.get.sh` and `route.guard.round.await.sh` in that repo
- related: #711 (the cache defect skill 1 surfaced)
